name: Sundering Shadows
english_description: An English-language, still-live fantasy LPMud (admin'd by leondal/Tlaloc) built on a heavily customized, Nightmare/TMI-lineage mudlib base, with a ~43,000-file/47MB archive that auto-commits from the live game every 30 minutes. Ships a full command-driven (not input_to-based) 15-stage character-creation wizard in d/shadowgate/setter_object.lpc (class, gender, race, subrace, template, age, stat rolling, body/hair/eye color, language, alignment, deity, class-special), a scripted basic-commands tutorial, and a large 1990s-2020s-vintage world tree. Porting it surfaced a wide range of genuine driver-dialect bugs: a pervasive same-file forward-reference gap (this driver resolves function calls in one pass per file, unlike the archive's assumed two-pass compiler; ~2,973 genuine sites needed forward declarations after de-duplicating against the ~65% the authors had already handled), the MudOS/LDMud map_delete() dialect (this driver's is void/in-place, not return-the-mapping; 245 files renamed off the m_delete() alias, plus 9 files/20 sites assigning its result), and dozens of one-off 'stray or missing type' bugs (bare `int *foo()` with a scalar body, `varargs foo(...)` missing its return type entirely so the compiler infers `unknown`, empty-array literals `({})` assigned to string/mapping-typed locals, TYPE-binding `int a, *b` sites). The single highest-impact find was in std/Object.lpc: set_short()/set_long() only accepted plain strings, but 291/20 call sites (including d/shadowgate/setter.lpc, literally the first room every new character enters) pass old-style closures for dynamic descriptions -- this silently broke every new registration from the room-entry point onward with no driver-visible crash, fixed by widening both setters to `mixed` and teaching query_short()/query_long() to evaluate a `functionp()` case, matching a calling convention already established elsewhere in the same file. A second, equally silent blocker was daemon/command.lpc's Nightmare-style command-dispatch table: its filename-to-verb parser sliced off a hardcoded 3 characters (correct for the archive's original `_verb.c` naming) to strip the leading `_` and extension, which silently truncated every single command name to garbage once this port's mechanical .c-to-.lpc rename lengthened every extension by two characters -- every ordinary player command (look, score, say, inventory, ...) failed with the driver's generic 'Why?' fail message and zero log signature, while add_action-registered verbs from character creation/rooms kept working, masking the bug until traced live via debug_message() instrumentation. Also fixed: daemon/multi_d.lpc's map_delete misuse blocking get_name() during registration, several missing runtime directories (log/player and siblings, daemon/save/saved_descriptions/<a-z>, d/save/quests) whose silently-aborting write_file()/save_object() calls aborted callers with no driver-level trace, a missing ansi_str() simul_efun (referenced by look/glance/spy with no implementation anywhere in the archive; added as a passthrough since this driver already auto-renders this mudlib's %^COLOR%^ markup at the write()/tell_object() layer), and one-off compile bugs in chat.lpc (IPC relay missing an argument), guilds_d.lpc, bonus_d.lpc, advance_d.lpc/titles.lpc/_scan.lpc (return notify_fail() used inside non-int-returning functions; this driver declares notify_fail void), holy_symbol_inherit.lpc (cleric/paladin holy-symbol logic), and a mage-class spellbook item. Verified end-to-end with a live driver and raw socket client: full registration through the 15-stage creation wizard, finalize, tutorial skip, and look/score/who/say/quit all producing correct output post-login. Left as documented gaps, not invented: /cmds/soul/atmos.lpc (the emote/soul-verb fallback daemon) is referenced but entirely absent from the archive, and a handful of specific monster/item files (magic_d.lpc's spell-school helpers, a knight NPC's paralysis override, an avenger NPC) still fail to compile behind non-core background daemons and were left for a future pass since they don't block registration or basic play.
